content: {"summary":"After the midnight rollout the fraud‑scorer pods showed higher CPU usage and throttling >25% while the number of gunicorn workers stayed the same. The rollout removed the WEB_CONCURRENCY setting, causing gunicorn to default to the node’s core count (16) workers, which exhausted the container’s CPU allowance early in each period.","likely_cause":"WEB_CONCURRENCY was unset in the new deployment, making gunicorn spawn workers equal to the node’s core count and driving CPU usage up, leading to throttling.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The rollout had WEB_CONCURRENCY unset, so gunicorn used the node’s 16‑core count for workers","evidence_ids":["INC-0030#2","INC-0024#2"],"quote":"With `WEB_CONCURRENCY` unset, gunicorn takes the visible CPU count, which on a 16-core node is 16"}],"next_checks":["Check the current deployment manifest for the WEB_CONCURRENCY environment variable","Confirm the number of gunicorn workers matches the intended concurrency setting","Monitor CPU usage and throttling after any future rollout that changes WEB_CONCURRENCY","Validate that CPU limits and requests are appropriate for the worker count"]}
